question: How strongly does the state economy during a governor's term (unemployment change, income growth, inflation) predict the governor's or their party's vote share when they next stand, and which measure do voters respond to most? Separately, how large is the incumbency advantage for governors and state legislators, before economic conditions are considered?

title: How much a governor's economic record moves their vote
usableAnswer: The change in vote share (percentage points) per percentage point change in state unemployment over the term, and per point of real income growth, with the study it comes from; whether voters weigh the last year more than the whole term; and the typical incumbency advantage in points for governors and for state legislators.
whyItMatters: Nothing an officeholder did counted when they ran again. Now the economy on their watch does, at a placeholder size. Too small and governing doesn't matter to reelection; too large and one bad draw ends a career.

answer.summary: Warshaw 2017 (preliminary; governor races 1969 to 2016): about +1.4 points of the governor's party's two-party share per 1 point better average annual wage and employment growth statewide; within a state-year at county level about 0.1 to 0.2; do not stack across indicators or months. Ebeid and Rodden 2006 (1950 to 1998): one-year unemployment change and real per-capita income, much weaker where farming or natural resources dominate. Rutgers: 498 of 668 incumbent governors who ran from 1948 to 2023 won (74.55%), a success rate, not a vote-share bonus. Uppal (lower houses in 45 states, 1968 to 1989, close races): about +5.3 points next-election share and about +30 points win probability (8.7 by the conventional method). The game's UNRESEARCHED_RECORD_IN_OFFICE values (60 support weight per point of unemployment change, capped at 150, on an 850 to 1150 draw) have no research validation and are not vote-share points. A calibration must keep four things apart: the officeholder's actions versus conditions during the term; party share versus personal incumbency; near-election versus whole-term record; election share versus starting-support weight.
answer.stillOpen: Whole-term unemployment coefficient, a transferable income coefficient, inflation, last-year versus whole-term weighting, and governor incumbency in vote-share points are all UNKNOWN. No game coefficient was selected.
